# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `go generate ./skills` from the command tree. Do not edit. -->

Every `maintainer` command in this release with its flags, as `--help` shows them.
Every command also accepts `-h, --help`.

## maintainer

An indispensable assistant for Open Source contribution.

```text
maintainer [command]
```

## maintainer fetch

Discovers GitHub repositories across owners and reconciles a local
checkout tree. Plan-only by default; --apply performs non-destructive
actions (clone, fetch, move, update-remote, adopt). Existing checkouts
and local work are retained.

```text
maintainer fetch [flags]
maintainer fetch [command]
```

Flags of every `maintainer fetch` command:

- `--concurrency int`: parallel discovery/clone cap (0 = from config)
- `--config string`: fetch config path (--config="" disables discovery)
- `--format string`: output format: human|json (default "human")
- `--owner strings`: limit this run to repositories of these owners; others are left alone (repeatable)
- `--profile strings`: limit this run to these profiles: repositories they list or track; others are left alone (repeatable)
- `-q, --quiet`: suppress everything below error on stderr
- `--timeout duration`: wall-clock budget for the whole command
- `--token string`: personal access token for the first selected profile
- `-v, --verbose count`: increase verbosity (-v, -vv, -vvv)

Flags of `maintainer fetch` itself:

- `--apply`: execute the plan (default: plan only)

## maintainer github

Allows to work with GitHub repositories and automate routine.

```text
maintainer github [command]
```

Flags of every `maintainer github` command:

- `--token string`: personal access token

## maintainer github contribution

Allows to look up the contribution calendar of the token owner,
to find a moment to contribute, and to keep and compare snapshots of it.

The calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API, which requires a token
even for a public profile: set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token. Only diff of two
snapshot files works without it.

A date of lookup and suggest that is empty or git is the author date of HEAD
in the current repository, or in the one GIT_DIR points to; outside
a repository, or in one without commits, it is now.

```text
maintainer github contribution [command]
```

Examples:

```sh
maintainer github contribution lookup 2022/+10
maintainer github contribution suggest --short
maintainer github contribution snapshot 2013 > snap.json
maintainer github contribution diff snap.json 2013
```

## maintainer github contribution diff

Compares the base and the head day by day and shows every day that
differs: the count in the base, the count in the head, and the signed
difference, e.g., +4 or -3. A day one of them lacks counts as zero there
and is shown as "-", so such a day is listed only if it has contributions. A line under
the table names the days only one of them covers.

Each argument is a year, YYYY, to fetch its contributions now, or a file
made by snapshot. Two files need no token; a year does:

The contribution calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API for
the owner of the token, which is required even for a public profile:
set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token.

```text
maintainer github contribution diff
```

Examples:

```sh
maintainer github contribution diff /tmp/snap.01.2013.json /tmp/snap.02.2013.json
maintainer github contribution diff /tmp/snap.2013.json 2013
```

## maintainer github contribution histogram

Shows a histogram of the contributions of the token owner: a row per
count of contributions, with a "#" per day that has it.

The argument is YYYY for the year, YYYY-MM for the month, or YYYY-MM-DD for
the week of the day, from Sunday to Saturday; without it, the current week.
The period is cut at now, a period in the future is an error, and the year
is not before 1970. The row of days without contributions is shown only
with --with-zero.

The contribution calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API for
the owner of the token, which is required even for a public profile:
set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token.

```text
maintainer github contribution histogram [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--with-zero`: shows zero-counted rows

Examples:

```sh
maintainer github contribution histogram
maintainer github contribution histogram 2013
maintainer github contribution histogram 2013-11
maintainer github contribution histogram --with-zero 2013-11-20
```

## maintainer github contribution lookup

Shows the contribution calendar of the token owner as a table:
a column per week, a row per day, and the distribution of the shown days
by the count of contributions under it.

The argument is date[/weeks]. The date is empty, git, now, YYYY, YYYY-MM,
YYYY-MM-DD, or RFC 3339; YYYY and YYYY-MM are the anchor at the first day,
not the whole year or month. An empty date or git is the author date of HEAD
in the current repository, or in the one GIT_DIR points to; outside
a repository, or in one without commits, it is now. The weeks add to the week
of the date: +N after it, -N before it, or N/2, rounded down, on each side,
so an even N shows N+1 weeks; without them it is -1, two weeks. N is at most
53, so the table shows up to 54 weeks, the year is not before 1970, and
a period in the future is an error. Days after now are shown as "?".

Weeks start on Sunday, and the week that contains January 1 is #01.

The contribution calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API for
the owner of the token, which is required even for a public profile:
set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token.

```text
maintainer github contribution lookup
```

Examples:

```sh
maintainer github contribution lookup
maintainer github contribution lookup 2013-12-03/9
maintainer github contribution lookup 2022/+10
maintainer github contribution lookup now/-4
```

## maintainer github contribution snapshot

Prints the contributions of the token owner for a year as a JSON object:
the count of contributions by the day, as RFC 3339 midnight UTC, including
the days without contributions. The result is a snapshot for diff.

The argument is YYYY, the current year without it. The year is cut at now,
a year in the future is an error, and it is not before 1970.

The contribution calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API for
the owner of the token, which is required even for a public profile:
set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token.

```text
maintainer github contribution snapshot
```

Examples:

```sh
maintainer github contribution snapshot > snap.json
maintainer github contribution snapshot 2013 | tee /tmp/snap.2013.json | jq
```

## maintainer github contribution suggest

Suggests the first moment between the anchor and now, both inclusive,
on a day with fewer contributions than its week requires: the most a day
of the week has, but not less than --target. A moment is within the
schedule, 05:00-19:00 UTC every day, and a random jitter of less than an
hour moves it neither after now nor after the schedule. The table of the
weeks around the suggestion marks its day with brackets in stderr, and stdout
gets only the timestamp, e.g., to pass it to git commit --date.

The argument is date[/weeks], the same as lookup has: the date is empty,
git, now, YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or RFC 3339, the weeks add to the week
of the date: +N after it, -N before it, or N/2, rounded down, on each side,
so an even N shows N+1 weeks; 5 without them, five weeks. The date is
the anchor; YYYY and YYYY-MM are anchored at the first day. An empty date
or git is the author date of HEAD in the current repository, or in the one
GIT_DIR points to; outside a repository, or in one without commits, it is
now. N is at most 53, so the table shows up to 54 weeks, and the year is not
before 1970.

It fails with a non-zero exit code if the anchor is in the future,
or if there is no suitable moment up to now.

The contribution calendar is read through the GitHub GraphQL API for
the owner of the token, which is required even for a public profile:
set GITHUB_TOKEN or pass --token.

```text
maintainer github contribution suggest [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--delta`: prints the suggestion relative to now, e.g., -3d2H0M0S
- `--short`: hides the table
- `--target uint`: the minimum contributions a day requires (default 5)

Examples:

```sh
git commit --date="$(maintainer github contribution suggest)"
maintainer github contribution suggest --delta 2013-11-20
maintainer github contribution suggest --target=5 2013/+10
maintainer github contribution suggest --short 2013-11/-10
```

## maintainer service

run the local maintainer service

```text
maintainer service [command]
```

## maintainer service run

Serves the local maintainer service over HTTP on loopback, at
http://maintainer.localhost:17841/ by default: the pages /status, /inbox and /tablo show
the checkouts of the collection and the issues mirrored in their
.github/issues and .github/roadmap, over the JSON API under /api/v0.
It reads service.toml from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/maintainer, else
~/.config/maintainer, and writes a commented default there when there is
none (--config names another file, which must exist), and the fetch
config and state as `maintainer status` does, with the home directory as
the working directory. It runs as your user and listens on 127.0.0.1 and
::1; a default address the system lacks, as ::1 with IPv6 turned off, is
skipped. listen in service.toml replaces the defaults, and --listen, which
may repeat, replaces both. SIGINT or SIGTERM stops it once the responses
in flight are sent. Do not run the mirror's export or push, or another
editor of the issue files, while triaging in the browser.

```text
maintainer service run [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--config string`: service config path (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/maintainer/service.toml)
- `--listen stringArray`: loopback address to listen on, repeatable; replaces the defaults (default [127.0.0.1:17841,[::1]:17841])

## maintainer skill

Shows or installs the agent skill for this release.

The skill teaches coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to use
maintainer. It ships inside the binary and matches its version. These
commands work offline, need no token and never read .env.

```text
maintainer skill [command]
```

## maintainer skill export

Write the skill into a directory, with an ownership marker next to SKILL.md.

A new or empty directory is written. --replace replaces a copy that maintainer
installed and nobody changed since; any other directory is left alone.

```text
maintainer skill export [flags]
```

Flags:

- `-o, --output string` (required): directory to write the skill into
- `--replace`: replace a copy that maintainer installed earlier

## maintainer skill info

print the skill's version, compatible range and digest

```text
maintainer skill info [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--json`: print one JSON object

## maintainer skill install

Install the skill for Claude Code or Codex.

Writes ~/.claude/skills/maintainer (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/maintainer) for
Claude Code and ~/.agents/skills/maintainer for Codex; with --project, the same
under the current directory. After upgrading maintainer, run it again with
--replace. A directory from another installer is left alone.

```text
maintainer skill install [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--agent strings` (required): agents to install for: claude-code, codex
- `--project`: install into the current directory instead of the user's skills
- `--replace`: replace a copy that maintainer installed earlier

Examples:

```sh
maintainer skill install --agent claude-code
maintainer skill install --agent claude-code,codex --replace
```

## maintainer skill show

print the skill's SKILL.md or one of its files

```text
maintainer skill show [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--file string`: file to print, e.g. references/cli.md (default "SKILL.md")

## maintainer skill status

Check the installed copies of the skill against this binary.

Looks in the user's and the project's skills of Claude Code and Codex, and
in their plugins. Fails when a copy is incompatible with this binary, was
changed after maintainer installed it, or no copy exists for a requested
--agent; with --exact, also when a copy differs from this release.

```text
maintainer skill status [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--agent strings`: agents to check: claude-code, codex (default all)
- `--exact`: also fail when a copy differs from this release
- `--json`: print one JSON record per copy

## maintainer status

Inspect local checkouts using fetch configuration and state. No network
access or fetch is performed; divergence uses cached upstream refs.
Lock marks remotes with a no_push push URL (the git lock marker).
In a terminal: arrows/jk select rows, Tab selects a column, s sorts,
Shift+s appends sorting, 0 resets sorting, / filters, q quits.

```text
maintainer status [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--concurrency int`: parallel Git inspection cap (default: fetch config)
- `--config string`: fetch config path (--config="" disables discovery)
- `--format string`: output format: auto|plain|json|tui (default "auto")
- `--owner strings`: limit rows to these owners (repeatable)
- `--root string`: override the checkout scan root
- `--timeout duration`: wall-clock budget (0 = unlimited)

## maintainer version

Show application version.

```text
maintainer version
```
